label: Most blessed: a primitive predicate for having in itself the perfect good of an intellectual nature
term: most blessed (in se et ex se beatissimus; Lean `Primitives.MostBlessed`)
definition: PRIMITIVE. MostBlessed g: g has, in and from itself, the perfect good of an intellectual nature. After ST I q.26 a.1 (beatitude is the perfect good of an intellectual nature, and belongs to God in the highest degree). Counterexample: a stone (no intellectual nature); a human being in this life (an intellectual nature without its perfect good).
note: Explicitly identified primitive (Encode first). Open semantic obligation: a typed account of beatitude as possession of an intellectual nature's perfect good. The only constraint placed on it is the open bridge 'Whatever is PERFECT_2 and has intellect is most blessed'.
